title: Playwright Quiz
description: Revisit the key ideas in Playwright. Read each choice carefully. You can try the quiz again after reviewing the lessons.

questions.question: What page does this example use?
options: A small page created by setContent
questions.explanation: A browser test opens a page and checks what a person can do. setContent gives this test a tiny page without a website server. The test finds a visible heading named Library.

questions.question: Which part distinguishes this button?
options: Its position in a random list
questions.explanation: A role describes what an element does. A button role and its name make a locator that resembles how a person finds the control. The locator finds the Borrow button.

questions.question: What connects the label to the input?
questions.explanation: A label tells a person what an input is for. getByLabel uses that relationship. The input receives Moon and the value check passes.

questions.question: What confirms the action worked?
questions.explanation: click asks Playwright to perform a real user-like click. Check the visible result, not only that the click method returned. After the click, the button reads Done.

questions.question: What is better than a guessed sleep?
questions.explanation: Playwright locator assertions retry for a short time. This helps when a visible change happens after the action. The assertion checks for the exact visible text and can retry while waiting.

questions.question: How many list items are expected?
questions.explanation: A locator can match several elements. toHaveCount checks how many matches exist. The list has two items.

questions.question: Which action clearly requests the checked state?
questions.explanation: check sets a checkbox to checked. It is clearer than clicking when the desired state is known. The checkbox ends in the checked state.

questions.question: What is Large's stored value?
questions.explanation: A select input stores an option value. The label shown to people can differ from that value. The Large option is selected and its value is l.

questions.question: What does Tab move here?
questions.explanation: A keyboard test checks focus and key actions. It can reveal a control that works only with a mouse. Tab moves focus from the first button to the second.

questions.question: Who supplies this page?
questions.explanation: A route handler can provide a known response. The test controls the content without calling a real external service. The route handler supplies the whole page. No real books.test server is needed for this request.

questions.question: What should each test prepare?
options: A dependency on the previous test
questions.explanation: Each Playwright test normally gets a fresh browser context. A context separates saved state such as cookies between tests. This test starts from its own page fixture. Another test should arrange its own required data.

questions.question: What does a screenshot capture?
questions.explanation: A screenshot records visible state. It helps explain a failure but is not a replacement for a precise behaviour check. The test checks the heading and saves a screenshot in the local test project.
